title: Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: Ventia Personnel
tiers.description: Ventia's Directors and Ventia Group employees. Bound by the insider trading prohibition, Ventia-imposed dealing bans, the Front Page Test, the short-term and speculative dealing ban, the hedging prohibitions and the section 3.6 margin lending approval requirement, but not by Blackout Periods or general prior approval.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Ventia Group employees. Used in the clearance table as the class whose approver is the Group CEO.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Ventia Directors, Key Management Personnel named in the Remuneration Report, Senior Executives (first, second and third line reports to the Group CEO) and Nominated Employees advised by the Group Company Secretary. Additionally subject to Blackout Periods, prior written clearance for every Dealing, and responsibility for Connected Persons.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Ventia Directors. Restricted Persons who clear through the Board Chairman and must notify the Group Company Secretary after any Dealing so Ventia can meet its ASX and NZX disclosure obligations.

tiers.name: Board Chairman
tiers.description: The Board Chairman, distinguished only for clearance: the approver is the Chair of the Audit, Risk and Compliance Committee.

tiers.name: Group CEO
tiers.description: The Group CEO, distinguished only for clearance: the approver is the Board Chairman.

tiers.name: KMP
tiers.description: Key Management Personnel as named each year in Ventia's Remuneration Report; a category of Restricted Persons with no separate substantive rules.

tiers.name: Senior Executives
tiers.description: Senior management, being any other first, second and third line reports to the Group CEO; a category of Restricted Persons with no separate substantive rules.

tiers.name: Nominated Employees
tiers.description: Other persons who regularly possess inside information and who have been advised by the Group Company Secretary that they are subject to special restrictions; a category of Restricted Persons with no separate substantive rules.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: A family member who may be expected to influence or be influenced by the Restricted Person (spouse, partner, children, partner's children, dependants) and any company or other entity, such as a trust, the Restricted Person has an ability to control.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may specify 'any other period' as a Blackout Period for Restricted Persons (4.1). Separately, under 3.1 Ventia may notify Ventia Personnel that they must not deal, either for a specified period or until the Group Company Secretary gives further notice. The policy does not say whether either is announced or confidential.

rules.detail: There is no express derivatives rule, but Securities is defined to include rights to acquire or dispose of securities and derivatives and other financial products under section 1042A whose value is linked to Ventia securities, with no venue limitation, and Dealing includes buying, selling or agreeing to buy or sell a Security. An OTC put and written call are therefore Dealings requiring prior clearance and are barred in Blackout Periods.
rules.evidence: derivatives and other financial products covered by section 1042A of the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) (Corporations Act) whose price or value is linked to the price or value of any of the securities referred to in (i) to (v) above

rules.detail: Employees who are not Restricted Persons are outside sections 4.1 and 4.3, so they need no clearance and are not bound by Blackout Periods; a derivative over vested unrestricted Securities is constrained only by the insider trading ban, any Ventia dealing notice, the Front Page Test and the speculative dealing ban.
rules.evidence: Certain parts of this Policy apply only to Restricted Persons

rules.detail: Absolute ban, applying to all Ventia Personnel and with no approval or exceptional-circumstances route, on hedging Securities acquired under any employee, executive or director equity plan before vesting.
rules.evidence: Securities acquired under an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by Ventia must never be hedged prior to vesting.

rules.detail: Vested plan Securities still subject to a holding lock or dealing restriction under the plan terms may never be hedged. The locks are created by plan documents outside this policy.
rules.evidence: Securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by Ventia.

rules.detail: The two hedging prohibitions are confined to unvested and locked plan Securities, so hedging other Securities is not banned. For a Restricted Person it is still a Dealing in Securities requiring prior written clearance, outside a Blackout Period, and must satisfy the Front Page Test. Unlike some peer policies there is no notification duty for executives who hedge.
rules.evidence: During any period that is not a Blackout Period, Restricted Persons must, prior to any proposed trade, seek approval for the proposed Dealing in Securities in accordance with section 4.4.

rules.detail: Hedging of Securities that are neither unvested plan Securities nor subject to a plan holding lock is left permitted for all Ventia Personnel; only the two plan-related states are prohibited.
rules.evidence: Securities acquired under an employee, executive or director equity plan operated by Ventia must never be hedged prior to vesting.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, collar-plus-loan or similar structure involves agreeing to sell Securities and dealing in a linked financial product, so it is a Dealing requiring clearance. Section 3.3 gives forward contracts as the example of prohibited short term dealing, which is the main obstacle to a forward-settled structure.
rules.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling Securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

rules.detail: Short selling is named as an instance of prohibited speculative dealing and is banned for all Ventia Personnel, with no approval route.
rules.evidence: Ventia Personnel must not Deal in Securities on a speculative basis e.g. short-term trading or short-selling.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not regulated. Borrowing securities appears only in the descriptive definition of short selling, and lending Ventia Securities is neither named nor caught by the definition of Dealing, which is limited to buying, selling, subscribing and agreeing to do so.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Ventia Securities is a financial product whose value is linked to the Securities and so a Security in its own right, but dealing in it would be speculative dealing, and a short CFD would fall within the short-selling ban.
rules.evidence: Ventia Personnel must not Deal in Securities on a speculative basis e.g. short-term trading or short-selling.

rules.detail: Margin lending is permitted rather than banned, for all Ventia Personnel including Directors, subject to approval through the section 4.4 written request process. Both entering a margin lending arrangement in respect of Securities and transferring Ventia Securities into an existing margin loan account need approval, and Ventia may impose conditions, expressly including conditions about when Securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call.
rules.evidence: Approval must be obtained in accordance with the procedure set out in section 4.4 for any: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of Securities; and transferring Securities in Ventia into an existing margin loan account.

rules.detail: Granting security, a charge, mortgage or pledge over Securities is not named and is not within the definition of Dealing. The only encumbrance-adjacent control is the section 3.6 approval requirement for margin lending arrangements, and there is no disclosure obligation for encumbered holdings.

There is no general prohibition on secured financing over Securities. Section 3.6 subjects margin lending arrangements in respect of Securities to approval, and a loan secured on Ventia shares with a maintenance or top-up mechanic would prudently be treated as within that phrase. Section 5 expressly contemplates a secured lender holding and enforcing over Securities.
rules.evidence: a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

rules.detail: A three month buy-sell window test extended by an open-ended ban on 'other short term dealings', with forward contracts given as the example. Selling Securities within three months of vesting under an equity plan is carved out, as are the section 5 Excluded Dealings.
rules.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling Securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts). Selling Securities received following the vesting of entitlements under an employee, executive or director equity plan within 3 months of the vesting date is not a short-term dealing.

exemption_authority: The section 4.2 exceptional circumstances route only: a Restricted Person may apply through the Group Company Secretary for approval to Deal in a Blackout Period on evidence of severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order, and the section 4.4 approver decides. There is no power to waive the section 3.4 hedging prohibitions or the section 3.3 speculative and short-term dealing ban, and any dealing allowed under section 4.2 must still comply with the rest of the Policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Approval must be obtained in accordance with the procedure set out in section 4.4 for any: entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of Securities; and transferring Securities in Ventia into an existing margin loan account.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Ventia regulates rather than prohibits borrowing against its shares, so the loan leg of a funded collar has an approval pathway instead of an outright bar, and the same approval route covers moving existing shares into a lender's account.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Ventia may, at its discretion, make any approval granted in accordance with section 4.4 conditional upon such terms and conditions as Ventia sees fit (for example, with regard to the circumstances in which Securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The company can dictate the enforcement mechanics of the facility as a condition of approval, so a bank should expect its close-out and top-up rights to be negotiated with Ventia before the facility is signed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Sections 3.3, 4.1 and 4.3 of this Policy do not apply to ... a disposal of Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Enforcement by the bank over the collared shares, including during a Blackout Period, is an Excluded Dealing needing no clearance, which materially de-risks the security package.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities means ... any rights to subscribe for, acquire or dispose of securities (including future contracts, options, performance rights, share rights or other interests); derivatives and other financial products covered by section 1042A ... whose price or value is linked to the price or value of any of the securities referred to in (i) to (v) above.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no venue limitation, so an OTC put and call written with a bank are themselves Securities and dealing in them is squarely within the clearance requirement and the Blackout Periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term trading includes buying and selling Securities on market within a 3 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Forwards are the named example of prohibited short term dealing, so a collar should run well beyond three months and avoid a prepaid-forward characterisation or short-dated roll structure.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approver is not obliged to provide reasons for any aspect of their decision and may revoke their approval at any time prior to the Dealing. ... the approved Dealing ... must occur within 2 business days following approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both legs and the facility drawdown must be executed inside two business days of clearance, and clearance can be pulled without reasons at any point before signing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Approval will not be granted to Ventia Personnel to Deal in Ventia Securities where the Dealing would not satisfy the Front Page Test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar can be refused purely on perception grounds even where no substantive rule is breached, and there is no appeal or reasons requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure that their Connected Persons only Deal in Securities in circumstances where the Restricted Person to whom they are connected would be permitted to Deal under this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the collared parcel through a controlled trust or company does not escape the clearance requirement, the hedging bans or the margin lending approval.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains a Front Page Test but no substance over form or anti-avoidance provision.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike several peer policies, Ventia has no express anti-avoidance hook to recharacterise a collar-plus-loan, so the analysis turns on the literal wording of sections 3.3, 3.4 and 3.6.

summary: A funded collar is achievable at Ventia over vested Securities that are free of any plan holding lock, and this is one of the more permissive policies in the market. Both derivative legs are Dealings, because Securities expressly includes derivatives and linked financial products with no venue limit, so a Restricted Person needs a written Clearance to Trade approved by the Board Chairman (for Directors) or the Group CEO (for employees), obtained outside the two results Blackout Periods, executed within two business days and revocable without reasons; a Director must also notify the Group Company Secretary the same day. The loan leg is not prohibited: section 3.6 subjects margin lending arrangements in respect of Securities, and transfers of Securities into an existing margin loan account, to the same approval process, Ventia may condition that approval on the margin call and sale mechanics, and section 5 treats a secured lender's enforcement sale as an Excluded Dealing even in a Blackout Period. The binding constraints are that unvested plan Securities and vested Securities still under a holding lock can never be hedged, with no exemption power, and that section 3.3 bans short term dealing and names forward contracts as its example, so the collar should have a tenor well beyond three months and avoid forward-sale characterisation. Practically, the bank should expect Ventia to negotiate the enforcement and top-up terms of the facility as conditions of approval.
